title: oneDNN
subtitle: Patches to Intel's math library for a GPU architecture the ecosystem had not caught up with, each one held to bit-identical output.

stats.label: special-value combinations behind the exact-arithmetic rewrite

lede: ActiveKV serves a 27-billion-parameter hybrid recurrent-attention open-weight model on one Intel Arc Pro GPU, and on that card prefill and the 4-bit-weight model path run their large matrix multiplications through Intel's oneDNN. The Intel Arc Pro GPU is a new architecture and the open kernel stack had gaps. I decided to patch oneDNN's own sources inside Intel's toolchain image, so the binary matches what the serving engine loads, and to gate every change on bit-identical output against the unpatched path, measured on the whole workload on a quiet benchmark host. The gate exists because of what sits above oneDNN: ActiveKV's exact mode must match fully resident attention bit for bit.
quote: A GEMM patch that moved a single bit would void every parity result built on it.
evidence: Intel GPU and SYCL/oneAPI engineering: oneDNN patched inside Intel's toolchain image for Xe2, one added GEMM catalogue entry cutting cold 32,000-token prefill from 21.54 s to 17.23 s.
Bit-exact numerical verification: every vendor-library patch gated on bit-identical output against the unpatched path, measured on the whole workload on a quiet host.
LLM quantization (4-bit): a tighter W4A16 lowering in oneDNN, and an exact instruction-set arithmetic rewrite tested across 48 special-value combinations and kept at flat speed.
author: Corey James
